display.purpose: Leaves only — posters, heroes, countdowns. The chrome never goes above Headline.

headline.purpose: The page h1. One per page, and the only large size in the chrome.

title.purpose: A species heading, and the largest type inside any card.

body.purpose: Everything readable. 65–75ch in prose columns; container-width in cards.

label.purpose: Uppercase 0.14em small caps — the recurring signal that a piece of type is chrome, not content.

micro.purpose: The smallest real step — the figure inside a count chip, and dense numeric furniture inside leaves. A label on a fill, never prose.

code.purpose: File paths, tokens, CLI verbs. Monospace for code, data and measurement only — never as a costume.

extensions.shadowPolicy: The chrome has no shadow vocabulary. Depth is a 1px hairline border plus a tonal step between plate and card. Shadows exist inside a few leaves as part of their own look and never migrate into the chrome.

motion.name: reading-position
motion.purpose: The house driver. Chrome motion is scrubbed by where the reader is, never by a clock; nothing autoplays.

motion.name: ease-measure
motion.purpose: Scrubbed motion that is a measurement — a count, a tally, a progress readout.

motion.name: ease-arrive
motion.purpose: Scrubbed reveals, so they resolve early rather than still arriving while being read.

motion.name: ease-house
motion.purpose: The decel curve for larger discrete transitions (300–500ms). Never bounce or elastic.

motion.name: duration-feedback
motion.purpose: Timed acknowledgement of a hover or focus, moving at most 2px.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Kills travel, autoscroll and repetition; keeps colour and opacity transitions, which are the ones carrying meaning. The arrived state is always the static state.

breakpoints.name: @lg
breakpoints.purpose: Container query. Converted from a 640px viewport minus ~128px of page chrome.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport. Site chrome only — a harvestable component may never use it.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport. Site chrome only — the width at which the lab gains its left gutter.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single filled action on a card or panel. Its accessible name carries the subject, never just the verb.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary span { transition: transform 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:hover span { transform: translateX(2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--ring); }

components.name: Specimen Card
components.description: The recurring unit of the whole site: a hairline white rectangle whose every figure is counted off disk. One link, its hit area stretched over the card.

components.css: .ds-card-specimen { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; list-style: none; background: var(--card); color: var(--card-foreground); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 12px; padding: 20px; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: border-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-card-specimen:hover { border-color: var(--primary); } .ds-card-specimen:focus-within { border-color: var(--ring); } .ds-card-specimen h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--foreground); } .ds-card-specimen-desc { margin: 4px 0 0; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-card-specimen-meta { margin: 12px 0 0; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-card-specimen-foot { margin-top: auto; padding-top: 16px; } .ds-card-specimen-action { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 8px; text-decoration: none; transition: opacity 150ms ease-out; } .ds-card-specimen-action::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 12px; } .ds-card-specimen-action:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-card-specimen-action:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--ring); }

components.name: Species Chip
components.description: A pill means 'a token of something enumerable', never 'a button'. Selected fills with the creator's primary; unselected is a hairline outline.
components.html: Motion 1Narrative 2Chrome 3
components.css: .ds-chiprow { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-chip-species { border: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--card); color: var(--muted-foreground); font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 9999px; text-decoration: none; transition: color 150ms ease-out, border-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-chip-species span { margin-left: 8px; font-size: 0.75rem; opacity: 0.7; } .ds-chip-species:hover { border-color: var(--primary); color: var(--primary); } .ds-chip-species:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-chip-species.is-current { border-color: var(--ring); background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); }

components.name: Count Chip
components.description: The understory voice: a non-interactive quantitative badge. Ink on accent, never white.
components.css: .ds-chip-count { display: inline-block; background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-foreground); font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 9999px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Rail Item
components.description: One tree in the forest rail: name, count chip, and a two-line clamped description. The current item takes a translucent primary wash rather than a solid fill.
components.html: TemporalCountdown4Time remaining until a fixed instant.Step Reveal3A sequence that advances on its own and can be steered.
components.css: .ds-rail { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; background: var(--card); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 12px; padding: 12px; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-rail-species { padding: 0 8px 4px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-rail-item { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 8px; text-decoration: none; transition: border-color 150ms ease-out, background-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-rail-row { display: flex; width: 100%; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-rail-name { flex: 1; min-width: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--foreground); } .ds-rail-desc { font-size: 11px; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-rail-item:hover { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 40%, transparent); background: var(--muted); } .ds-rail-item:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--ring); } .ds-rail-item.is-current { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 40%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 10%, transparent); } .ds-rail-item.is-current .ds-rail-name { color: var(--primary); } .ds-chip-count { display: inline-block; background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-foreground); font-size: 10px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 9999px; }

components.name: Header Navigation
components.description: A baseline row of small links. The current page is the creator's primary; the rest are muted ink resolving to foreground on hover.
components.html: 🌲 the forestlabprimergithub
components.css: .ds-header { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-header nav { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 24px; padding: 16px 24px; } .ds-header-brand { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--foreground); text-decoration: none; } .ds-header-link { font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--muted-foreground); text-decoration: none; transition: color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-header-link:hover { color: var(--foreground); } .ds-header-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-header-link.is-current { color: var(--primary); } .ds-header-external { margin-left: auto; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Editor-dock scale: small, hairline, 6px. The caret, selection and accent colour are themed globally rather than per field.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input { background: var(--card); color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-family: inherit; caret-color: var(--primary); accent-color: var(--primary); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--ring); } .ds-input::selection { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); }

components.css: @property --tally { syntax: "<integer>"; inherits: false; initial-value: 0; } .ds-stats { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 24px; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-stats dt { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-tally { --tally: var(--tally-to); counter-reset: tally var(--tally); margin: 0; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--foreground); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } @supports (animation-timeline: view()) { @media not (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-tally { animation: ds-tally-count linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 20% cover 45%; } .ds-tally::before { content: counter(tally); } .ds-tally > span { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; } } } @keyframes ds-tally-count { from { --tally: 0; } }

narrative.overview:
This is a naturalist's catalogue, not a product. The site is a neutral plate on which specimens are mounted, labelled, and looked at — and the specimens are forty leaves that each argue loudly for their own look. Every decision in the chrome follows from that division: the plate is flat, hairline-ruled, small-capped, and almost entirely uncoloured, so that a brutalist poster leaf and a glass page-nav leaf can sit two cards apart without the page taking a side.

The unusual constraint here is that the palette does not belong to this site. Five values — --primary, --primary-foreground (derived, never stored), --accent, --ring, --background — plus the font are ambient CSS on a wrapper, and a creator moves them. Every colour in the token set is a resting value: what the platform looks like before anyone has touched it. A component styled only in card / border / muted is not neutral, it is deaf to the creator, and it fails without crashing.

Density is high and unapologetic. This is a working surface for two people who already know the vocabulary — a curator and a coding agent — and the readability budget is spent on getting more of the forest on screen, not on marketing air.
keyCharacteristics: Flat plate, hairline structure — 1px borders and tonal steps, no shadows in the chrome
A repaintable palette: five movable values, everything else fixed
Small-caps labels at 11px with 0.14em tracking as the recurring signal of 'this is chrome, not content'
Rounded-xl cards, rounded-full chips, generous internal padding, nothing lifted
Derived everything — no stored nav, no arrangeable sections, no hand-written list of species
Motion driven by reading position, never by a clock

rules.name: The Five Movable Things Rule
rules.body: A creator can move exactly --primary, --primary-foreground (derived from the accent, never stored), --accent, --ring, and --background, plus the font. Never add a sixth. Never invent a component-scoped variable to get around it — theming is inherited, and a component that defines its own theming variable has re-invented the mechanism the wrapper already provides.

rules.name: The Deaf Leaf Rule
rules.body: Every component must reach for primary, accent, or ring somewhere. One styled purely in card / border / muted / foreground is not tastefully restrained — it is invisible to the creator's brand, and it fails silently because nothing crashes. This is a test, not a guideline.

rules.name: The Derived Foreground Rule
rules.body: A primary fill is always bg-primary + text-primary-foreground. bg-foreground and text-background are banned outright: they name tokens editor mode never touches, so a call to action painted in them stays platform-coloured on every creator page. White-on-accent is not safe to assume — a lime accent puts white text at 1.91:1, and even the platform's own default pink needs black.

rules.name: The Raw Letterform Rule
rules.body: Never paint a letterform in the creator's raw colour: bg-clip-text + text-transparent is banned, because --primary-foreground is derived against a ground and clipped text has no ground at all. The single exception is a wordmark that draws its own keyline around every glyph.

rules.name: The Tracking-Follows-Size Rule
rules.body: Small caps get looser as they get smaller: 0.14em at label size, 0.18em–0.3em for the tiniest eyebrows inside leaves. Large type goes the other way — tracking-tight at Title and above, never wider.

rules.name: The Tabular Numeral Rule
rules.body: Any figure that changes in place — a count, a countdown, a scrubbing tally — is tabular-nums. Numerals that reflow while they animate read as a bug.

rules.name: The Own-Box Rule
rules.body: A leaf measures its own box, never the window. Every root a leaf can render carries @container, and every breakpoint is a container query — sm: / md: / lg: fail the conformance suite by shape, not by list. A component is dropped into whatever column its consumer has and is never told how wide the window is; a viewport rule fails silently. The one exception is a fixed viewport overlay, which really is the window.

rules.name: The Flat-Plate Rule
rules.body: If a chrome surface needs to read as separated, give it a border or a tonal step. If that is not enough separation, the layout is wrong — reach for space before reaching for a shadow.

rules.name: The No-Coloured-Slab Rule
rules.body: No border-left accents above 1px, no hard offset shadows, no gradient fills in the chrome. A surface is a hairline rectangle on a tonal ground; if it needs emphasis, it gets an indigo border, not a costume.

rules.name: The Reading-Position Law
rules.body: Motion is driven by where the reader is, not by a clock. Nothing autoplays. Scrubbed motion is linear when it is a measurement and ease-out when it is an arrival. The arrived state is the static state: every keyframe is a from, so reduced motion, an unsupported browser, or a stylesheet that never loads all land on a finished page.

dos: Do style every component in primary / accent / ring somewhere, so a creator's colour can reach it.
Do pair a primary fill with text-primary-foreground, always — it is derived for contrast against whatever the creator picked.
Do measure a component's own box with @container queries and the house viewport→container mapping; give a fixed overlay @container too.
Do carry structure with a 1px Hairline border and a tonal step, and reach for space before reaching for a shadow.
Do use the 11px / 0.14em uppercase label as the signal that a piece of type is chrome rather than content.
Do put exactly one filled action on a surface, and give its accessible name the subject.
Do set tabular-nums on any figure that changes in place.
Do let motion be driven by reading position, and make the arrived state the static state.
donts: Don't add a sixth movable value, a theme prop, or a component-scoped CSS variable. Theming is inherited ambient CSS.
Don't paint a fill in bg-foreground or text in text-background; don't clip a gradient into a letterform without a drawn keyline.
Don't use dark:, a hex literal, or a Tailwind palette colour (text-slate-500) anywhere a semantic token exists.
Don't use sm: / md: / lg: in a component that can be harvested — those are the site's chrome's privilege alone.
Don't introduce a shadow, gradient, or coloured slab into the site's chrome; leaf-level depth stays inside the leaf.
Don't grow the marketing furniture of a design system site or a component-library showcase: no swatch grids, no gradient hero, no 'trusted by', no copy-the-class-name affordances.
Don't add a dark-mode toggle. The theme follows prefers-color-scheme and nothing else.
Don't hand-write a list of species, a stored layout, or a curation surface. If a link is not derivable from the folder layout, it does not belong in the nav.
Don't put an interactive target below 24px: text under text-xs on a control needs an explicit height or a hit area carried past the drawn box.
Don't ship an interactive element without a focus-visible treatment — the UA outline does not look broken, which is exactly why it gets missed.
